Ultra-realistic, cinematic, faceless short-form video that takes the viewer on a single continuous first-person journey: a panicked sprint to and through the door of a modest, mysterious structure in a dramatic remote place, a brisk walk to a staircase, a continuous POV descent down that staircase, and a calm off-POV reveal of a hidden, secret, luxurious living space concealed below it.

The video must be composed for a vertical 9:16 frame and must always remain upright, never sideways or horizontal.

The video ALWAYS follows the same fixed five-beat format — only the setting, the structure, and the hidden interior change between episodes:
1. FIRST-PERSON POV at FULL-TILT SPRINT — the lone traveler runs STRAIGHT AT the structure's entrance DOOR and THROWS HIMSELF at it BODY-FIRST. The video opens already in full-tilt motion: the runner is sprinting flat out across a dramatic remote setting toward the door. K0 must have the DOOR AT 20–25 METRES AHEAD, CENTERED IN THE FRAME as the dominant focal point — the runner's path leads DIRECTLY to it. The world RUSHES PAST at real sprint speed (~6–7 m/s) — ground flying past beneath, terrain at the frame edges blurring from forward motion. The runner is FOCUSED on the door (it stays the focal point throughout the clip) but the path is mildly non-linear, weaving slightly around obstacles, with 1–2 brief shoulder-glances backward then snapping back to door focus. As the runner reaches the door, his BODY (chest/shoulder) SLAMS into it — NOT his hand reaching from a distance, NOT slowing — and the door YIELDS INWARD INSTANTLY (swings AWAY from the camera INTO the structure) under his momentum. He continues forward INTO the structure WITHOUT BREAKING STRIDE, WITHOUT PAUSING, WITHOUT ANY FRAME OF STILLNESS. By the end of scene 1 (K1) the runner is INSIDE the FIRST ROOM (the modest interior of the structure — e.g. inside the shed, cabin, hut, bunker, lighthouse base), facing INTO THE ROOM (NOT facing the doorway), mid-stride forward, with the interior of the first room as the dominant view ahead and the staircase to the lower level visible somewhere ahead in the room.
2. FIRST-PERSON POV — purposefully and briskly walking ACROSS the first room interior toward the top of a normal STRAIGHT STEP STAIRCASE descending below. The first room is humble (wooden plank floor or rough concrete or stone tile, plain walls). The camera FACES FORWARD INTO THE ROOM, with the staircase becoming the focal point as the runner approaches it. He is still hurrying (purposeful brisk pace, NOT calm). By the end of scene 2 (K2) he is AT THE TOP of the straight step staircase, the camera angled DOWNWARD into the descending steps — the staircase dominates the frame, going DOWN into warm light from below.
3. FIRST-PERSON POV — CONTINUOUS DESCENT down the straight step staircase from top to bottom. The camera stays in POV the entire clip — it NEVER lifts off the head, NEVER cuts to a third-person view, NEVER skips ahead, NEVER teleports. The camera is angled DOWNWARD throughout, watching the steps roll past beneath as he walks down them one by one. Per-step bob: camera dips as each foot lands on the next step down, with a brief settle, then the next step. Warm amber light grows brighter as he descends toward the lower room. The pace can ease slightly here — he is reaching safety. By the end of scene 3 (K3) he is at the BOTTOM step or just stepping off it into the lower room — the camera at the bottom of the stairs, the lower room (the hidden luxury interior) visible AHEAD as the camera transitions from looking-down at steps to looking-forward into the room.
4. OFF-POV (third-person) FIRST REVEAL of the hidden luxurious interior. The camera switches to off-POV positioned IN THE LOWER ROOM, looking across the room. The traveler — seen only from behind or in profile, face NEVER shown, clothing/body LOCKED — has just emerged from the staircase and is walking calmly in ONE consistent forward direction across the room (e.g. from the staircase area toward the next room's archway), unbothered, going about his life. The camera slowly TRACKS LATERALLY (smooth horizontal dolly) across the room as he walks. The staircase entrance is a SUBTLE, SECONDARY element at ONE edge of the frame — only the bottom 1–2 steps and the wall opening visible, with the higher steps cut off out of frame; the man is IN the lower room, NOT on the staircase. The hidden luxury interior is the dominant feature of the frame.
5. OFF-POV (third-person) HOUSE-TOUR — the traveler walks toward and through an open archway or doorway into ANOTHER luxurious room of the hidden residence — same materials, lighting palette, and continuity as the lower room (physically consistent residence). The camera follows him from behind in one smooth continuous house-tour move. His clothing, body, silhouette, and gait are IDENTICAL to scene 4.

CAMERA: Scenes 1–3 are real FIRST-PERSON POV — a body-cam or chest-mounted GoPro on the traveler. Scene 1 is EXTREME body-cam shake (a panicked sprint that ends with a body-slam through the door, world rushing past at sprint speed). Scene 2 is a hurried brisk walk across the first room with reduced bob. Scene 3 is the CONTINUOUS POV DESCENT — step-by-step bob down the staircase, never lifts off the head. Scenes 4–5 are calm off-POV third-person — the traveler is seen only from behind or in profile, face NEVER shown, clothing/appearance LOCKED. The POV-to-off-POV transition happens cleanly between scenes 3 and 4, at the bottom of the descent when the man has stepped off the last step into the lower room.

RUNNING & MOVEMENT MUST LOOK REAL — highest priority and a persistent weakness. In scene 1 the camera must JOLT EXTREMELY DOWN-UP and side-to-side with EACH footfall in a FAST sprint cadence (about 3–4 strides per second — a flat-out sprint, NOT a jog). The frame rotates 8–15 degrees per stride before recentering. Motion blur at frame edges from speed. Panicked panting breath audible. CRUCIAL FOR REAL-SPRINT FEEL: the WORLD MUST RUSH PAST the camera at high speed — the ground FLIES past beneath, terrain at the edges RACES past as a blur from forward motion (NOT a slow approach with shake on top — that reads as 'fake walking with shake'). First-person POV keyframes (scenes 1-3) use a natural human eye- or chest-level first-person composition with slightly imperfect, casual framing — like a real frame grabbed from body-cam footage. The traveler's body is not visible (no arms, legs, torso, reflection) except S1 forearms may occasionally appear briefly at the BOTTOM edge of the frame (not exaggerated, not the focus).

K0 keyframe: the structure's entrance DOOR is at 20–25 METRES AHEAD, CENTERED IN THE FRAME as the dominant focal point — clearly visible as a real door, NOT a tiny dot, NOT to the side. The runner's straight-ahead path leads DIRECTLY to this door. The dramatic remote setting fills the surroundings. The runner is at the start of the approach, body not visible (POV), pre-sprint instant.

Scene 1 keyframe (K1): a POV view from INSIDE the FIRST ROOM (the modest interior of the structure — humble materials, plain walls, wooden plank floor or rough concrete or stone tile). The camera FACES FORWARD INTO THE ROOM — the first room's interior is the dominant view AHEAD, with the staircase to the lower level VISIBLE somewhere ahead in the room. The doorway through which the runner just entered is BEHIND the camera and OUT OF THE FOCAL POINT — at most a small partial peripheral hint at ONE side edge of the frame. NEVER framed facing the doorway. NEVER framed with the outside view dominating.

Scene 2 keyframe (K2): a first-person POV looking DOWN into the top of a real STRUCTURALLY-ATTACHED straight step staircase descending below into warm light — treads on stringers attached to the side walls, the stairwell enclosed (rock/concrete/wood/stone), warm amber light from below. The staircase dominates the frame. NEVER stairs going up, NEVER a ladder, NEVER floating steps, NEVER an outdoor window in the stairwell.

Scene 3 keyframe (K3): a POV view at the BOTTOM step or just stepping off it into the lower room. The camera is at the bottom of the stairs, transitioning from looking-down-at-steps to looking-forward into the lower room interior. The last 1–2 steps may be visible at the bottom of the frame; the lower room (hidden luxury interior) is visible ahead as the dominant feature. The traveler's body is not visible (POV).

Scene 4 keyframe (K4): an OFF-POV (third-person) composition IN THE LOWER ROOM — the camera is positioned in the room, looking across it. The lone traveler is IN the room (NOT on the staircase) seen from behind or in profile (face never shown), walking calmly in ONE consistent forward direction across the room. The staircase entrance is a SUBTLE, SECONDARY element at ONE edge of the frame — only the bottom 1–2 steps and the wall opening visible, the higher steps CUT OFF out of frame. The hidden luxury interior is the dominant feature of the frame.

Scene 5 keyframe (K5): an OFF-POV third-person composition in ANOTHER luxurious room of the hidden residence — the traveler from behind walking through or having just walked through an open archway/doorway into this second room; clothing and body IDENTICAL to K4; the second room richly furnished with materials and palette CONSISTENT with the lower room.

Use natural, real-weather lighting outside (K0) and motivated, plausible lighting inside the first room (K1, K2), the stairwell (K2-K3), and the lower room (K3-K5). Avoid postcard-perfect or stock-photo polish in the exterior keyframe.
No on-screen text, numbers, subtitles, logos, or watermarks anywhere in the frame.

Any handrail visible in the stairwell keyframes (K2 / K3) is on the SIDE WALL only, NEVER in the middle/centerline of the staircase. The staircase is structurally attached to the side walls and floor — NEVER floating, NEVER unsupported.
continuity_rules: Maintain the locked structure identity across K0 and K1: the same structure, surroundings, weather, time of day, and materials/colors established in K0 are consistent with the structure type in K1.

Each keyframe must visibly advance the journey a believable short step from the previous one — door centered at 20–25m (K0) → INSIDE FIRST ROOM facing INTO room with staircase visible ahead (K1) → at TOP of staircase looking DOWN (K2) → POV at BOTTOM of stairs looking forward into lower room (K3) → OFF-POV in lower room with traveler walking across (K4) → OFF-POV in another room (K5) — never a near-duplicate, never a teleport, never a backwards step.

Keep exactly one traveler. In POV keyframes (K0, K1, K2, K3) his body is invisible (camera is his eyes/chest) except S1 forearms occasionally in the lower frame of K1; in K4 and K5 he is seen only from behind or in profile, face never shown, CLOTHING/BODY/HAIR/SILHOUETTE IDENTICAL across K4 and K5.

Consecutive keyframes must share recognizable visual anchors (the structure, the door, the first room, the staircase, the lower-room walls, the floor materials) so the video generator can interpolate a smooth, believable forward move.

The door is the same physical object across K0 (closed, centered, 20–25m ahead) and end-of-S1 (yielded inward under the body-slam) — same thickness, material, hardware; it opens INWARD fast under the body's impact and stays open; it never opens outward, never vanishes.

K1 FACING: the K1 keyframe MUST face INTO the first room (interior dominates the frame), with the doorway BEHIND the camera and out of the focal point. NEVER framed facing the doorway. NEVER framed with the outside view dominating.

The staircase shown in K2 (from above) and K3 (POV at bottom) is the SAME physical staircase — a normal STRUCTURALLY-ATTACHED straight step staircase going DOWN. NEVER a ladder, vertical ladder, rungs, spiral, circular, or helical staircase. NEVER floating steps. NEVER going up. The staircase entrance at the edge of K4 is the bottom of this same staircase, with only the lowest 1–2 steps visible.
The stairwell is fully enclosed in every keyframe in which it appears — no outdoor windows.
Any handrail in K2 or K3 (or the K4 edge) is on the SIDE WALL only, never in the middle of the staircase.

INTERIOR CONSISTENCY across K4 and K5 (and the lower-room start in K3): same lower-room walls, ceiling, floor, furniture, lighting, palette, and materials in EVERY frame; NO floating elements, NO shape-shifting, NO morphing geometry.
PERSON CONSISTENCY across K4 and K5: the lone traveler has IDENTICAL clothing, body, hair/hood, height, gait, and silhouette in every off-POV frame.
Every keyframe is exactly ONE single photographic frame — never multi-frame, multi-panel, storyboard, grid, triptych, split-view, or before-and-after.

K0 and K1 are radically different framings — K0 outside with the door CENTERED at 20–25 metres ahead; K1 INSIDE the FIRST ROOM with the camera FACING INTO the room (NOT facing the doorway, NOT facing outside).
No on-screen text, numbers, or logos in any keyframe.

camera_rules: Scenes 1-3 are first-person POV (body-cam/GoPro/handheld) — body never visible (forearms may occasionally appear briefly in the bottom of S1's frame). Scenes 4-5 are calm off-POV third-person — the traveler is seen only from behind or in profile, face never shown.

Scene 1 camera = BODY-CAM on a PANICKED sprinting runner FLEEING through the setting STRAIGHT AT the door (centered at 20–25m in K0): EXTREME footstep bob per stride (3–4 strides per second flat-out sprint), horizon dipping, rising, AND tilting per stride, frame rotating 8–15 degrees per stride, motion blur at frame edges, WORLD RUSHING PAST at sprint speed (~6–7 m/s — ground flies past beneath, terrain races past blurred at edges), per-stride surge-and-settle, panicked panting breath, door REMAINS the dominant focal point with brief 1–2 shoulder-glances backward (camera not always away from the door, just brief glances), forearms occasionally and briefly at the bottom of the frame (NOT exaggerated), AND at the end the runner BODY-SLAMS the door (body-first, not hand-reach), the door yields INWARD instantly (swings away from camera into the structure), and the runner BARGES THROUGH without pausing into the first room FACING INTO THE ROOM. NEVER tracking shot, forward tracking shot, dolly, gimbal, Steadicam, smooth tracking, walking-with-shake, constant-forward-glide, gliding, floating, weightless, skating, jogging, straight-line, or exaggerated arm movement.

Scene 2 camera = POV brisk hurried walk across the first room to the top of the descending staircase: reduced bob compared to S1, still handheld, camera facing FORWARD INTO the room throughout (NEVER turning back toward the doorway), ending at the top looking DOWN into the stairs.

Scene 3 camera = POV CONTINUOUS DESCENT — stays in POV start-to-end, angled DOWNWARD, watching steps roll past beneath, per-step bob downward, NEVER lifts off the head, NEVER cuts to third-person, NEVER skips ahead, NEVER floats through stairs, NEVER passes through walls, NEVER has a wall open up.
Scene 4 camera = off-POV third-person in the lower room — a slow, smooth horizontal lateral tracking shot from one side of the room to the other while the traveler walks IN the room (not on stairs).
Scene 5 camera = off-POV third-person follow from behind the traveler as he walks through into another room — smooth continuous house-tour move.

All modes ban a fake floating/weightless camera, teleporting, environment morphing, impossible moves, rotated/sideways framing, any mid-clip switch between POV and third-person (except the clean S3→S4 boundary at the bottom of the descent), any mid-clip change of person direction/appearance in S4-S5, any pause/stop at the door in S1, any K1 facing the doorway/outside, and any floating-through-stairs or wall-opening-up in S3.
Camera motion must never be used to paper over a mismatch between keyframes; the move must be the natural one for the stated mode.
motion_rules: The dominant motion in scene 1 is real PANICKED FLEEING sprint plus a body-slam through the door at the end — a real person running flat out STRAIGHT AT the centered door (20–25m in K0) at 3–4 strides per second, hard pounding footfalls, panicked panting breath, the body-cam jolting EXTREMELY DOWN-UP and side-to-side per stride with frame rotation per stride, WORLD RUSHING PAST at sprint speed (~6–7 m/s), per-stride surge-and-settle biomechanics, door remaining the dominant focal point with brief 1–2 shoulder-glances, forearms occasionally in the lower frame (not exaggerated), AND at the end the runner BODY-SLAMS the door (body-first, not hand-first), the door yields INWARD instantly, and the runner barges through without slowing into the first room FACING INTO the room. NEVER smooth, NEVER gliding, NEVER skating, NEVER jogging, NEVER walking-with-shake, NEVER constant-forward-glide, NEVER exaggerated arm movement; NEVER feet sliding; NEVER a slow approach; NEVER opens outward; NEVER a pause at the door; NEVER K1 facing the doorway or outside.

Scene 2: hurried brisk POV walking across the first room interior to the top of the staircase; reduced bob from S1; camera FACING FORWARD INTO the room throughout (never turning back to the doorway); ends with the camera looking DOWN into the stairs.

Scene 3: POV CONTINUOUS DESCENT down a normal STRUCTURALLY-ATTACHED straight step staircase, step by step, from top to bottom in ONE continuous POV shot. Camera angled DOWNWARD throughout, per-step bob with each footfall on the next step DOWN. NEVER a ladder, rungs, spiral, circular staircase, or floating steps. NEVER climbs up. NEVER lifts the camera off the head mid-stairs. NEVER cuts to third-person. NEVER time-jumps or skips. NEVER floats through stairs. NEVER passes through walls. NEVER has a wall open up.

Scene 4: a slow, smooth, horizontal lateral tracking shot in the lower room while the traveler walks IN the room (not on stairs) in ONE consistent forward direction, unbothered. NEVER turns around, NEVER reverses, NEVER walks backwards. Interior geometry LOCKED. Person appearance LOCKED.
Scene 5: a smooth, continuous follow from behind as the traveler walks through into another luxurious room. Person appearance IDENTICAL to S4.

Exactly one traveler moves. In POV (scenes 1-3) his body is unseen except S1 forearms occasionally; in scenes 4-5 he is seen only from behind or in profile, face never shown, appearance LOCKED across both.
Natural elements (waves, rain, fog, wind, snow) move with real physics and match the weather established in K0.
Any handrail in the stairwell is on the SIDE WALL only — never in the middle of the staircase, never intersecting the traveler's body.
No teleporting, morphing, melting, floating objects, time-jumps, walls opening up, or physically impossible transformations. Every clip depicts ONE continuous motion from start to end.

Audio is natural diegetic sound only, matched exactly to the visible action — and EVERY clip's audio directive must name the SPECIFIC surface material being walked or run on for footstep sounds. NEVER music, score, or dramatic sound design.

metadata.title_prompt: Generate a short, curiosity-driven title for a cinematic faceless POV video that journeys through a dramatic remote place into a hidden, secret, luxurious living space. Build intrigue and awe WITHOUT spoiling the reveal — never describe the final interior. Imply 'where does this lead?' or 'what is hidden out here?'. Match the specific setting and structure of this episode (coast, forest, cliff, lighthouse, etc.). Never mention AI or that it is generated. Maximum 90 characters.
metadata.description_prompt: Generate a short, intriguing description for a cinematic faceless POV journey that ends in a hidden secret luxury retreat. 1-2 sentences. Tease the mystery and the remote destination without spoiling the reveal. Natural and human, never AI-sounding. An optional light curiosity line is fine. Maximum 300 characters.
metadata.hashtag_prompt: Generate 6 to 10 relevant hashtags with no spaces, mixing cinematic / POV / hidden-places / secret-bunker / luxury-retreat / exploration tags with broader viral tags. Reflect the specific setting of this episode (coastal, forest, cliff, etc.).

audio.prompt: Audio must contain ONLY real, natural, diegetic environmental sound that matches exactly what is on screen. Never include music, soundtrack, background score, cinematic audio, ambient music, or dramatic sound design. The audio must feel like raw footage recorded on location. EVERY scene must include footstep sounds on a SPECIFIC named surface material (e.g. wet rocks, sand, gravel, snow, wooden plank floor, concrete, stone tile, creaking timber stairs, concrete stairs, stone steps, hardwood floor, deep rug) — vague or missing surface naming causes missing or wrong step sounds. Depending on the scene: HARD pounding running footfalls on the specific ground surface and panicked panting breath (S1), a BODY-SLAM thud and the door swinging inward with a metallic or wooden latch and creak at the end of S1, brisk walking footsteps on the specific first-room floor (S2), walking footsteps descending the specific staircase material (S3), calm walking footsteps on the specific lower-room floor and quiet warm room tone (S4-S5). Absolutely no music at any point.

memory.instruction: Review the list of previous videos carefully.
